title: One approval, many simultaneous users
scenario: 16 threads authorize the same approved action at the same instant.
expected: Exactly one allowed; no errors; audit chain verifies.

title: Approve and deny race
scenario: 20 times, the owner's approve and deny for the same approval arrive at the same instant.
expected: Exactly one decision wins each time; a denied approval never runs; chain verifies.

title: Duplicate approval and denial events
scenario: approve, approve, deny on one approval; deny, deny, approve on another (retried messages).
expected: Only the first decision counts ([T,F,F,T,F,F]); final states approved/denied; each refused repeat audited.

title: Concurrent approval requests
scenario: 20 threads each request 5 different approvals.
expected: 100 distinct ids, 100 pending rows, 100 request rows, chain verifies.

title: One pairing code raced by many nodes
scenario: 10 times, 10 threads trade the same one-time pairing code at once.
expected: Exactly one token per code, every time.

title: PIN guesses in parallel respect the limit
scenario: 30 wrong PINs for one approval are sent at the same instant over the owner plane.
expected: No more than PIN_TRIES (5) guesses are actually checked; the rest are refused 429.

title: Audit with two connections and many threads
scenario: Two Kernel instances on the same folder, 8 threads, 25 appends each.
expected: Chain verifies with exactly 200 events.

title: Audit with concurrent writer processes
scenario: 4 separate processes append 60 audit rows each at the same time.
expected: Chain verifies with exactly 240 events; all exit 0.

title: Process killed in the middle of audit writes
scenario: A writer process is SIGKILLed while appending in a tight loop.
expected: The chain verifies afterwards and the next append works.

title: Process dies inside a transaction
scenario: A process writes an approval and its audit row in one transaction, then exits before commit.
expected: Neither row exists afterwards; chain verifies.

title: Corrupt state database
scenario: state.db is replaced with random bytes.
expected: Kernel refuses to start (DatabaseError) and leaves the file untouched.

title: Half-truncated state database
scenario: state.db with 400 audit rows is cut to half its size.
expected: Either the kernel refuses to open it or verify() with the anchor fails; never 'ok'.

title: Connector allowlist cut off mid-write
scenario: connectors.local.json holds half a JSON document.
expected: Read as empty; a connector job is not_configured; nothing starts.

title: Projects allowlist corrupt
scenario: projects.json holds half a JSON document and a project_check job arrives.
expected: The job returns ok=false with an error class; no crash.

title: Damaged JSON rows do not break the owner plane
scenario: A job row with broken params/result, an audit row with broken payload and one approval with broken JSON.
expected: Job view 200 with result None; events 200; state 200 and still lists the good approval.

title: Database full during an approved action
scenario: SQLite hits its size limit (max_page_count) before an approved action is authorized; then space is freed.
expected: authorize raises (not allowed); chain verifies; after space returns a GREEN action is allowed and the chain still verifies.

title: Deep scrub with no usable temp folder
scenario: TMPDIR points to a missing folder (as on a full or broken disk) and a token goes through scrub(deep=True).
expected: No crash; the built-in pass still redacts the token.

title: Node output save on a full disk
scenario: The node saves an output while open() fails with ENOSPC.
expected: Result ok=false, error 'OSError'; no partial file left.

title: Repeated kill and resume
scenario: 50 kill/resume cycles with an action attempted in each state.
expected: Refused every time killed, allowed every time resumed; 50 kill and 50 resume rows; chain verifies.

title: Kill switch under load
scenario: 8 threads authorize in a loop; the owner kills the switch mid-way.
expected: No action that began after kill() returned is allowed; chain verifies.

title: Write lock held by a live process
scenario: Another process holds the SQLite write lock for 1.5 s.
expected: The kernel waits and the audit append succeeds (no 'database is locked').

title: Write lock left by a crashed process
scenario: A process takes the write lock, writes, and is SIGKILLed.
expected: The next writer proceeds within 5 s; its uncommitted row is gone; chain verifies.

title: Stale running command after restart
scenario: An owner command was 'running' when the kernel stopped.
expected: On restart it is failed with a 'restarted' error; the gate is free.

title: Stuck and abandoned jobs after a clock jump
scenario: A queued and a running job; the clock moves past both TTLs; then the node reports late.
expected: Queued -> expired, running -> failed; the late result is not accepted.

title: PIN lockout survives the clock going back
scenario: Five wrong PINs, then the system clock is set back an hour.
expected: Still 429 (fail safe); after the window really passes, the right PIN works.

title: Clock jump expires approvals
scenario: An approved action is used after the kernel's clock jumps forward past the TTL.
expected: Refused with 'approval expired'; history shows expired.

title: Malformed MCP tool results
scenario: process_result gets None, a list, str, int, bytes, content as dict/int/str, junk items, a non-dict resource, string isError, a set in structuredContent.
expected: No exception; every output is JSON-serialisable and marked untrusted.

title: Huge MCP tool result
scenario: A 5 MB text result.
expected: Truncated to about 16,000 characters, flagged truncated, in under 15 s including the gitleaks pass.

title: Binary and control characters in tool text
scenario: Text with NUL, ANSI escapes, a lone surrogate and PNG header bytes.
expected: No crash; result JSON-serialisable and untrusted.

title: Duplicate, foreign and oversized job results
scenario: The node reports a job twice, another node reports it, and a 200 KB result arrives for another job.
expected: First accepted only; others refused; oversized stored as 'result too large'.

title: Malformed requests to the node endpoint
scenario: Bad JSON, empty and oversized bodies, a JSON list, a string action, a bad job result and binary garbage, then a valid request.
expected: Each malformed one 4xx (bad job result accepted:false); the server keeps serving.

title: Guard proxy survives garbage connections
scenario: Empty, garbage, missing-port, bad-port and 20 KB NUL requests to the browser guard proxy.
expected: Still answers the next request (403 for a loopback target).

title: Overlapping calls to one connector
scenario: A second call arrives while the first connector call is still running.
expected: The overlap gets 429 busy; first and later calls 200; the server saw 2 calls.
